# Annual QA/QC Pipeline {.unnumbered}

## Introduction

This document runs one project year's raw lab files through ingestion, QA/QC evaluation, WQX formatting and CDX export. Everything year-specific is read from `config.yml`, `year_files/` and `reference/`.

The structure of Part C follows the Data Evaluation Checklist provided by the Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation. Results that fail QA/QC are marked Rejected before upload to the EPA Water Quality Exchange (WQX); they remain in the public record.

Question tags in Part C (AUTO, MANUAL, MIXED) are provisional and show how much of each answer the pipeline can compute. Chunks marked `eval: false` are not yet ported from `project_year/2025.qmd`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Setup

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(janitor)
library(lubridate)
library(here)

config <- yaml::read_yaml(here("config.yml"))
source(here("functions", "check_config.R"))
check_config(config)
year <- config$year

# format_wqx.R expects the spring date as M/D/YYYY
spring_d <- ymd(config$sampling$spring_date)
spring_sample_date <- sprintf("%d/%d/%d", month(spring_d), day(spring_d), year(spring_d))

cfg <- list(
  year                  = year,
  templates_dir         = here("reference/wqx_templates"),
  wqx_template_file     = here("year_files", paste0("AWQMS_KWF_Baseline_", year, ".xlsx")),
  wqx_intermediate_path = here("output/intermediate", paste0(year, "_kwf_baseline_results_wqx.csv")),
  flagged_export_path   = here("output/intermediate", paste0(year, "_export_data_flagged.csv")),
  flag_decisions_path   = here("year_files", paste0(year, "_data_flag_decisions.csv")),
  planned_samples_path  = here("year_files/planned_samples.xlsx"),
  # Moves into the template layout when the repo is blanked (Phase E)
  wqx_downloads_dir     = here("other/input/WQX_downloads"),
  activity_media_name   = config$wqx$activity_media_name,
  activity_media_subdivision_name = config$wqx$activity_media_subdivision_name,
  spring_sample_date    = spring_sample_date,
  summer_sample_date    = config$sampling$summer_date
)

dir.create(here("output/intermediate"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Pipeline Run

Required order: planned-samples gate, combine_dat, assess_lab_qc, assign_qc_status, assess_holding_times, format_wqx, apply_qaqc_flags, generate_cdx_export. The `format_wqx.R`, `apply_qaqc_flags.R` and `generate_cdx_export.R` scripts read and write the global environment.

The planned-samples gate reads `year_files/planned_samples.xlsx` (what was planned for this year, filled in before the run) and stops the run, listing every problem, until the workbook is complete. Q23, Q25 and Q26 use the same plan.

```{r pipeline, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
fn_files <- c("resolve_rm_site", "numeric_utils", "clock_utils", "check_dat_contract",
              "ingest_sgs", "ingest_fc", "ingest_tss", "ingest_ysi", "combine_dat",
              "assess_lab_qc", "assign_qc_status", "assess_holding_times",
              "planned_samples")
for (f in fn_files) source(here("functions", paste0(f, ".R")))

planned_plan <- check_planned_samples(read_planned_samples(cfg$planned_samples_path))
planned <- expand_planned_samples(planned_plan)

res <- combine_dat(config)
lab_qc <- assess_lab_qc(res$lab_qc)
qc <- assign_qc_status(res$dat, res$sample_batches, lab_qc, config$qc$blank_multiple)
dat <- qc$dat
# Row key shared with format_wqx.R, which keeps an existing dat_row
dat$dat_row <- seq_len(nrow(dat))
lab_qc_actions <- qc$lab_qc_actions

# Q17 hold times feed the QC status, so they are assessed before the export is finalized
holding_times <- assess_holding_times(
  dat,
  read.csv(file.path(cfg$templates_dir, "sample_holding_times.csv")),
  read.csv(file.path(cfg$templates_dir, "in_situ_methods.csv"), colClasses = "character")
)

source(here("functions/format_wqx.R"))
source(here("functions/apply_qaqc_flags.R"))

# The CDX export needs station and project downloads from WQP; skip when absent
wqp_project_file <- file.path(cfg$wqx_downloads_dir, "project/project.csv")
if (file.exists(wqp_project_file)) {
  source(here("functions/generate_cdx_export.R"))
} else {
  message("generate_cdx_export skipped: WQP downloads not found in ", cfg$wqx_downloads_dir)
}

# Inputs for prelim_report.qmd
write.csv(export_dat, here("output/assessed_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(lab_qc, here("output/lab_qc_assessed.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

**17.) Were preservation, hold time and temperature requirements met?**

Hold time is the elapsed time from collection to the start of analysis, compared with `reference/wqx_templates/sample_holding_times.csv`. In-situ meter readings are Not applicable. A missing time of day is bracketed (earliest and latest possible elapsed time); a row is Not evaluable only when the answer depends on the missing value, or when the method has no limit in the table. A result that exceeds its limit is Rejected in the export (reason `Hold time exceeded`). Lab receipt is not used in the calculation; it is cross-checked only (collection, receipt and analysis must be in order).

```{r q17-holdtimes}
holding_times |>
  filter(hold_status != "Not applicable") |>
  summarise(
    results = n(),
    limit_hours = first(max_hold_hours),
    max_elapsed_hours = if (all(is.na(elapsed_hours))) NA_real_ else max(elapsed_hours, na.rm = TRUE),
    pass = sum(hold_status == "Pass"),
    fail = sum(hold_status == "Fail"),
    not_evaluable = sum(hold_status == "Not evaluable"),
    .by = c(lab_name, epa_analysis_id)
  )
```

```{r q17-exceptions}
holding_times |>
  filter(hold_status %in% c("Fail", "Not evaluable") | receipt_check == "Out of order") |>
  select(sample, analyte, lab_name, epa_analysis_id, elapsed_hours, max_hold_hours,
         hold_status, hold_note, receipt_check)
```

The table above is empty when every evaluable result passed and every recorded receipt is in order.

```{r q17-receipt}
holding_times |>
  filter(receipt_check != "Not applicable") |>
  count(lab_name, receipt_check)
```

Receipt times for the wastewater treatment plant samples (fecal coliform and TSS) are sometimes hand-written on the chain of custody, so they are entered by hand in `config.yml` (`rec_date`, `rec_time`). "Not recorded" above means that entry is blank. Sample temperature at receipt and preservation are not in the lab data tables; confirm them against the laboratory receipt documentation and chain of custody and record the finding in the text below.

```{r q17-preservation}
dat |>
  filter(!epa_analysis_id %in% read.csv(file.path(cfg$templates_dir, "in_situ_methods.csv"),
                                        colClasses = "character")$analytical_method) |>
  distinct(lab_name, epa_analysis_id, result_sample_fraction, preservative) |>
  arrange(lab_name, epa_analysis_id)
```

MANUAL: receipt temperature and preservation finding (not yet written for this year).

**18.) Are dissolved metal quantities less than total metals quantities?**

For every characteristic measured in both fractions at the same location and date (primary samples only), the dissolved result is compared with the total result. A Dissolved result comes from a filtered sample and a total result from an unfiltered one (SGS flags these `L` and `.` in its data deliverable; `Total` and `Unfiltered` are both treated as total). Results are compared in ug/L. A pair is Not comparable when either result is a non-detect or below the quantification limit. Dissolved above total is reported in two tiers: within tolerance, when the relative percent difference is no larger than the duplicate RPD limit for that characteristic (`rpd_threshold()`), or exceeding tolerance. The tolerance is a project convention; the QAPP does not state one.

This comparison does not reject anything by itself. Every pair that exceeds tolerance needs a decision recorded in `year_files/{year}_data_flag_decisions.csv` (`flag` Y rejects, N accepts, with `notes`; a blank `result_sample_fraction` applies to both results). The pipeline stops before the export until each exceedance has a decision.

```{r q18-summary}
dt_pairs |>
  count(characteristic_name, dt_status) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = dt_status, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
```

```{r q18-exceptions}
dt_pairs |>
  filter(startsWith(dt_status, "Dissolved >")) |>
  select(monitoring_location_id, activity_start_date, characteristic_name, unit,
         dissolved_result, total_result, rpd_pct, threshold, dt_status)
```

The table above lists every pair with dissolved above total; it is empty when there are none.

```{r q18-decisions}
dt_pairs |>
  filter(dt_status == "Dissolved > total (exceeds tolerance)") |>
  left_join(
    read.csv(cfg$flag_decisions_path, colClasses = "character") |>
      mutate(activity_start_date = mdy(activity_start_date)) |>
      select(monitoring_location_id, activity_start_date, characteristic_name,
             result_sample_fraction, decision = flag, notes),
    by = c("monitoring_location_id", "activity_start_date", "characteristic_name")
  ) |>
  select(monitoring_location_id, activity_start_date, characteristic_name,
         result_sample_fraction, decision, notes)
```

MANUAL: interpretation of any dissolved-above-total pairs and the decision rationale (not yet written for this year).

<br>

**19.) Are the duplicate sample(s) RPD (Relative Percent Difference) within range described in QAPP?**

Each original and field duplicate pair is evaluated under two rules side by side (`assess_rpd()`): QAPP v3, the rule this project operates under, and the ADEC 2026 QAPP guidance. Under QAPP v3, RPD is used only when one or both results are above the LOQ and one or both are at least 2x the LOQ; otherwise the pair is Not evaluable. ADEC 2026 differs for results below the LOQ: RPD is skipped when the other result is under 2x the LOQ, and the pair fails when the other result is at least 2x the LOQ. Non-detects arrive with value 0. RPD limits are those of QAPP v3 Tables 4 and 5: 20% for metals, 25% for nutrients, 5% for suspended solids.

Fecal coliform has no precision criterion in QAPP v3 Table 5 (only sterility and temperature checks), so its pairs are shown with the RPD and the status No criterion, and they never reject results. This is a project decision; a criterion should be written into the next QAPP (`topics/qapp_revision_notes.md`).

A pair that fails under QAPP v3 rejects both the original and the duplicate result in the export (reason `Field duplicate RPD fail (QAPP v3)`). The exception is a failing pair in which one result is below the LOQ (for example a detect against a non-detect). Those pairs need a decision recorded in `year_files/{year}_data_flag_decisions.csv` (`flag` Y rejects both results, N accepts, with `notes`); the pipeline stops before the export until each has one, and they are rejected only on Y.

```{r q19-summary}
rpd_pairs |>
  summarise(pairs = n(), .by = c(qapp_v3, adec_2026)) |>
  arrange(qapp_v3, adec_2026)
```

```{r q19-by-analyte}
rpd_pairs |>
  summarise(
    pairs = n(),
    limit_pct = first(threshold),
    pass = sum(qapp_v3 == "Pass"),
    fail = sum(qapp_v3 == "Fail"),
    not_evaluable = sum(qapp_v3 == "Not evaluable"),
    no_criterion = sum(qapp_v3 == "No criterion"),
    .by = c(characteristic_name, sample_fraction)
  ) |>
  arrange(characteristic_name, sample_fraction)
```

```{r q19-exceptions}
rpd_pairs |>
  filter(qapp_v3 == "Fail" | adec_2026 == "Fail" | !rules_agree) |>
  select(monitoring_location_id, activity_start_date, characteristic_name, sample_fraction,
         result_orig, result_rep, loq, rpd_pct, threshold, qapp_v3, adec_2026, needs_decision)
```

The table above lists every pair that fails under either rule, or on which the two rules disagree. `needs_decision` is TRUE for pairs that wait on a decision.

DECISION PENDING: dissolved lead at 10000015 on 7/23/2025 (original 7.36 ug/L, replicate not detected, LOQ 2, DL 0.5) fails both rules with one result below the LOQ. A Y or N row is needed in `year_files/2025_data_flag_decisions.csv` before the pipeline can reach the export.

**20.) Were there any laboratory discrepancies, errors, data qualifiers, or QC failures (review laboratory duplicates, matrix spikes and blanks)?**

The laboratory QC records (`lab_qc`: blanks, laboratory control and fortified samples, matrix spikes and duplicates, calibration checks, surrogates) are assessed by `assess_lab_qc()` against the limits the laboratory reports with each record; nothing is hardcoded. A record is Fail if any applicable check fails, Pass if at least one check passes and none fail, and Not evaluable otherwise (including a missing limit). Low-level QC (LLQC) records carry no recovery limits from SGS, so they are Not evaluable here.

Blanks are assessed under two rules side by side: the QAPP v3 rule (primary; any detection above the detection limit fails) and the ADEC 2026 rule (fails at or above the LOQ). Only the QAPP rule sets the record's result.

A failed record rejects results through `assign_qc_status()`, by scope:

- Batch controls (LCS, LCSD, CCV, ICV and similar): every result in the same batch with the same laboratory, method, analyte and fraction.
- Blanks: detected results in the same batch, method, analyte and fraction that are below `blank_multiple` times the blank result. The multiple is a project convention set in `config.yml`; the QAPP does not state one.
- Matrix spikes and duplicates: the parent sample only.

The Rejected results themselves are reported under Q21.

```{r q20-summary}
lab_qc |>
  count(lab_name, qc_group, qc_result) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = qc_result, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  arrange(lab_name, qc_group)
```

```{r q20-fails}
lab_qc |>
  filter(qc_result == "Fail") |>
  select(lab_name, season, qc_group, sample_type, sample_id, analyte, analytical_method,
         qc_check, result, resultflag, units, loq, dl, percent_recovered, rec_limit_low,
         rec_limit_high, sample_rpd, rpd_limit_high, anl_batch)
```

The table above lists every failed laboratory QC record; it is empty when there are none.

```{r q20-blank-rules}
lab_qc |>
  filter(qc_group == "blank") |>
  count(lab_name, blank_qapp, blank_adec) |>
  arrange(lab_name, blank_qapp, blank_adec)
```

```{r q20-actions}
lab_qc_actions
```

The table above shows, for each failed record, its scope, how many results it matched (`n_matched`) and how many were Rejected (`n_rejected`).

```{r q20-qualifiers}
dat |>
  filter(!is.na(resultflag)) |>
  count(lab_name, resultflag) |>
  arrange(lab_name, resultflag)
```

Result flags above are the laboratory's own (`=` detected, `J` estimated between the detection limit and the LOQ, `U` not detected). Laboratory narrative notes, discrepancies and errors are not in the data tables; review the laboratory reports and record the finding below.

**21.) Is any laboratory data rejected and why?**

A result is Rejected when any of these apply: a failed laboratory QC record (Q20), a blank fail (Q20), a field duplicate RPD fail under QAPP v3 (Q19), a decision recorded as Y in `year_files/{year}_data_flag_decisions.csv` (Q18, Q19), or a missed holding time (Q17). `finalize_qc_status()` combines them, so `export_dat` holds each result's final `qc_status` and every reason in `qc_fail_reason`. Rejected results stay in the export with a flag; they are not deleted.

```{r q21-summary}
export_dat |>
  count(activity_type, qc_status) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = qc_status, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(percent_rejected = round(100 * Rejected / (Accepted + Rejected), 1))
```

```{r q21-reasons}
# A result can carry several reasons, so the rows below can sum to more than the Rejected count
reason_patterns <- c(
  "Blank fail" = "^Blank fail|; Blank fail",
  "Lab QC fail" = "Lab QC fail",
  "Field duplicate RPD fail" = "Field duplicate RPD fail",
  "Hold time exceeded" = "Hold time exceeded",
  "Manual flag" = "Manual flag"
)

rejected <- export_dat |>
  filter(qc_status == "Rejected")

tibble(
  reason = names(reason_patterns),
  results = map_int(reason_patterns, \(p) sum(grepl(p, rejected$qc_fail_reason)))
) |>
  add_row(reason = "Other (not matched above)",
          results = sum(!Reduce(`|`, map(reason_patterns, \(p) grepl(p, rejected$qc_fail_reason)))))
```

```{r q21-by-analyte}
rejected |>
  count(characteristic_name, result_sample_fraction, name = "rejected") |>
  left_join(
    export_dat |> count(characteristic_name, result_sample_fraction, name = "total"),
    by = c("characteristic_name", "result_sample_fraction")
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(rejected))
```

```{r q21-list}
rejected |>
  select(monitoring_location_id, activity_start_date, activity_type, characteristic_name,
         result_sample_fraction, result_value, result_unit, qc_fail_reason)
```

The table above lists every Rejected result with the reason(s); it is empty when none are rejected. Each blank-fail reason names the blank, its result and its batch.

MANUAL: discussion of the rejected data (not yet written for this year).

**22.) During the field season, review raw data files (EDDs, instrument records) as they are received. Document changes and corrections to methods as needed.**

Raw files are read once, by the ingest functions, and are never edited. Every change made on the way in is listed below, derived from the data, so the list stays complete without a hand-written note.

Site labels. SGS labels resolve through `sgs_site_names_matching_table.xlsx` (a lookup, not a correction). Other labs' labels resolve by river mile in `resolve_rm_site()`, which accepts underscores and tolerates spacing and letter-for-zero typos. The table shows each label that was not already in the form `RM <number>` or `RM <number> DUP`.

```{r q22-site-labels}
dat |>
  filter(lab_name != "SGS", grepl("^RM", sample), !grepl("^RM [0-9.]+( DUP)?$", sample)) |>
  distinct(lab_name, sample, monitoring_location_id) |>
  mutate(change = if_else(
    grepl("^RM [0-9.]+( DUP)?$", gsub("_", " ", sample)),
    "Underscore read as space",
    "Spelling or spacing normalized"
  )) |>
  arrange(change, lab_name, monitoring_location_id)
```

Method names. `analytical_method_raw` holds the method exactly as the lab file reports it; `analytical_method` is the cleaned value used for the lookups.

```{r q22-methods}
dat |>
  filter(analytical_method != analytical_method_raw) |>
  count(lab_name, analytical_method_raw, analytical_method, name = "results")
```

The table above is empty when no method names were changed.

YSI value corrections. Reviewed values that were corrected before replicates were averaged, from `year_files/ysi_corrections.csv`; each row carries its reason.

```{r q22-ysi}
ysi_corrections_path <- here("year_files/ysi_corrections.csv")
if (file.exists(ysi_corrections_path)) {
  read.csv(ysi_corrections_path, colClasses = "character", na.strings = "") |>
    as_tibble()
} else {
  tibble(note = "No YSI corrections file for this year.")
}
```

The table above is empty when no values were corrected.

MANUAL: corrections made outside the code (lab reissues, hand-edited files, corrected copies such as `<name>_corrected.xlsx` with their `corrections_log` sheet) and any change to methods during the season (not yet written for this year).

**23.) Is the dataset complete and did you receive the expected number of results?**

Expected results come from `year_files/planned_samples.xlsx`, checked by the gate in the pipeline run. Expected = planned primary results plus planned field QC results (field duplicates, field blanks, trip blanks). Lab-internal QC (method blanks, LCS, matrix spikes) is not counted. The QAPP does not say whether planned field QC counts toward the expected total; see `topics/qapp_revision_notes.md`. Season is the sampling event nearest to each result's collection date. Every planned result not received counts as a shortfall.

```{r q23-compare}
# Final QC status lives in export_dat; dat_row links the two tables
planned_cmp <- compare_planned_to_dat(
  planned,
  dat |>
    select(-any_of(c("qc_status", "qc_fail_reason"))) |>
    left_join(select(export_dat, dat_row, qc_status), by = "dat_row"),
  config$sampling$spring_date, config$sampling$summer_date
)

planned_cmp |>
  summarise(
    planned  = sum(planned),
    received = sum(received) - sum(unplanned),
    missing  = sum(missing),
    .by = c(season, sample_type)
  ) |>
  mutate(sample_type = factor(sample_type,
                              c("Primary", "Field Duplicate", "Field Blank", "Trip Blank"))) |>
  arrange(season, sample_type)
```

The table above counts only planned results in `received`; results collected but not planned are listed separately below and stay out of the expected total.

```{r q23-totals}
planned_cmp |>
  summarise(
    planned  = sum(planned),
    received = sum(received) - sum(unplanned),
    missing  = sum(missing),
    .by = sample_type
  ) |>
  bind_rows(
    summarise(planned_cmp, sample_type = "All planned",
              planned = sum(planned), received = sum(received) - sum(unplanned),
              missing = sum(missing))
  )
```

Planned results not received, by season, sample type, analyte and fraction, with the river miles affected.

```{r q23-missing}
site_rm <- read_planned_samples(cfg$planned_samples_path)$sites |>
  transmute(monitoring_location_id = as.character(monitoring_location_id), river_mile)

planned_cmp |>
  filter(missing > 0) |>
  left_join(site_rm, by = "monitoring_location_id") |>
  summarise(
    missing     = sum(missing),
    river_miles = paste(sort(unique(river_mile)), collapse = "; "),
    .by = c(season, sample_type, analyte, sample_fraction)
  ) |>
  arrange(season, sample_type, desc(missing), analyte)
```

The table above is empty when no planned result is missing.

Results received but not planned (not counted in the expected total, and never raise the accepted count).

```{r q23-unplanned}
planned_cmp |>
  filter(unplanned > 0) |>
  left_join(site_rm, by = "monitoring_location_id") |>
  select(season, sample_type, river_mile, analyte, sample_fraction, unplanned) |>
  arrange(season, river_mile, analyte)
```

The table above is empty when every received result was planned.

**25.) Does project meet Completeness Measure A criteria?**

Measure A = Accepted results / results collected, for primary results only. The QAPP wording of this ratio is inverted; this definition is our interpolation (see `topics/qapp_revision_notes.md`). Goals are set in `config.yml` (QAPP and ADEC range).

Primary results are results from the routine environmental samples at each site and sampling event. They exclude field duplicates, field blanks and trip blanks (field QC samples), and lab-internal QC (method blanks, laboratory control samples, matrix spikes), which is kept in a separate table and never enters this measure. We chose primary results only because Measure A is meant to describe how much of the environmental data collected is usable. Field QC samples exist to evaluate data quality rather than to characterize the river, so counting them would let the pass rate of QC samples change the completeness of the environmental record. Field QC results are still counted in Measure B (Q26), through the same expected total used in Q23.

```{r q25}
completeness_tbl <- function(x, num, den, goal) {
  x |>
    summarise(n_num = sum({{ num }}), n_den = sum({{ den }}), .by = c(analyte, sample_fraction)) |>
    filter(n_den > 0) |>
    mutate(pct = round(100 * n_num / n_den, 1),
           meets_goal = n_num / n_den >= goal) |>
    arrange(analyte, sample_fraction)
}

cma_primary <- planned_cmp |> filter(sample_type == "Primary")

cma_overall <- cma_primary |>
  summarise(accepted = sum(accepted), collected = sum(received)) |>
  mutate(measure_a_pct = round(100 * accepted / collected, 1),
         goal_pct = 100 * config$completeness$goal_a,
         meets_goal = accepted / collected >= config$completeness$goal_a)
cma_overall

completeness_tbl(cma_primary, accepted, received, config$completeness$goal_a) |>
  rename(accepted = n_num, collected = n_den, measure_a_pct = pct)
```

The first table is the overall result and the second is by analyte and fraction. The goal is `goal_a` in `config.yml`; the ADEC range is shown there for comparison.

MANUAL: discussion of any analyte below the goal (not yet written for this year).

<br>

**26.) Does project meet Completeness Measure B criteria?**

Measure B = Accepted results / planned results, using the same expected total as Q23 (primary plus planned field QC). Only accepted results that were planned count in the numerator, so unplanned extras never raise the figure. The QAPP wording is inverted here too (see `topics/qapp_revision_notes.md`).

```{r q26}
cmb_overall <- planned_cmp |>
  summarise(accepted_planned = sum(accepted_planned), planned = sum(planned),
            .by = sample_type) |>
  bind_rows(
    summarise(planned_cmp, sample_type = "All planned",
              accepted_planned = sum(accepted_planned), planned = sum(planned))
  ) |>
  mutate(measure_b_pct = round(100 * accepted_planned / planned, 1),
         goal_pct = 100 * config$completeness$goal_b,
         meets_goal = accepted_planned / planned >= config$completeness$goal_b)
cmb_overall

planned_cmp |>
  filter(planned > 0) |>
  completeness_tbl(accepted_planned, planned, config$completeness$goal_b) |>
  rename(accepted_planned = n_num, planned = n_den, measure_b_pct = pct)
```

The first table is by sample type and overall; the second is by analyte and fraction, over all planned sample types.

**28.) Are the correct monitoring locations associated with the project? Are latitude and longitude filled out in a consistent format?**

Project policy: all results are submitted under the monitoring locations already registered in CDX (the sites in the approved QAPP). New locations are not created, because that would require a modified and re-approved QAPP. When the place actually sampled differs slightly from a registered location, the difference is described in a note and the registered location is still used.

`reference/baseline_sites.csv` is the single source of site coordinates for the whole pipeline: the locations and coordinates registered in CDX. The ingest contract check, the Activity Latitude and Longitude in the export, and this section all read it (its identifiers carry the `KENAI_WQX-` prefix, removed here to match the upload IDs; the contract check and `format_wqx.R` stop if a location is not in that file).

Places the crews actually sample that differ from a registered location are recorded by the user in `year_files/sampled_locations.csv` (columns `monitoring_location_id`, `sampled_latitude`, `sampled_longitude`, `notes`; a header-only file means no differences). Nothing in the pipeline can detect a changed sampling location, so fill this file in each year from field records. Entries that differ from the registered coordinates by more than the tolerance below are listed for your attention, because the QAPP coordinates no longer describe where samples are collected. Assumption: `baseline_sites.csv` holds the coordinates registered in CDX; it was last checked against the Water Quality Portal listing of the organization's locations on `r config$sites$verified_date` (set in `config.yml`; update it when you re-check) and should be re-checked whenever sites change. Every ID in `sampled_locations.csv` must exist in `baseline_sites.csv` (the render stops otherwise); IDs with no results this year raise a warning.

Format consistency: every coordinate in the export is taken from `baseline_sites.csv`, so all locations share one source and format. The checks below therefore test that each value is numeric, that longitude is negative, and that it matches the registered value, rather than comparing the number of decimal places.

```{r q28-check}
# Differences below this distance are treated as rounding
tolerance_m <- 10

haversine_m <- function(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) {
  rad <- pi / 180
  a <- sin((lat2 - lat1) * rad / 2)^2 +
    cos(lat1 * rad) * cos(lat2 * rad) * sin((lon2 - lon1) * rad / 2)^2
  round(2 * 6371000 * asin(sqrt(a)), 1)
}

ref_sites <- read_csv(here("reference/baseline_sites.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  transmute(
    monitoring_location_id = str_remove(MonitoringLocationIdentifier, "^KENAI_WQX-"),
    ref_lat = latitude, ref_lon = longitude, river_mile
  )

sampled_path <- here("year_files/sampled_locations.csv")
sampled_sites <- if (file.exists(sampled_path)) {
  read_csv(sampled_path, show_col_types = FALSE,
           col_types = cols(monitoring_location_id = col_character(),
                            sampled_latitude = col_double(), sampled_longitude = col_double(),
                            .default = col_character())) |>
    transmute(monitoring_location_id, sampled_lat = sampled_latitude, sampled_lon = sampled_longitude,
              sampled_note = notes)
} else {
  tibble(monitoring_location_id = character(), sampled_lat = double(), sampled_lon = double(),
         sampled_note = character())
}

unknown_sampled <- setdiff(sampled_sites$monitoring_location_id, ref_sites$monitoring_location_id)
if (length(unknown_sampled) > 0) {
  stop("year_files/sampled_locations.csv has IDs not in reference/baseline_sites.csv: ",
       paste(unknown_sampled, collapse = ", "))
}

site_check <- export_dat |>
  distinct(monitoring_location_id, activity_latitude, activity_longitude) |>
  mutate(
    monitoring_location_id = as.character(monitoring_location_id),
    lat = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(activity_latitude)),
    lon = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(activity_longitude))
  ) |>
  left_join(ref_sites, by = "monitoring_location_id") |>
  left_join(sampled_sites, by = "monitoring_location_id") |>
  mutate(
    in_reference   = !is.na(ref_lat),
    numeric_ok     = !is.na(lat) & !is.na(lon),
    # Kenai Peninsula, longitude west of Greenwich is negative
    sign_ok        = numeric_ok & lon < 0,
    export_matches = in_reference & numeric_ok & haversine_m(lat, lon, ref_lat, ref_lon) <= tolerance_m,
    sampled_differs = in_reference & !is.na(sampled_lat) &
      haversine_m(sampled_lat, sampled_lon, ref_lat, ref_lon) > tolerance_m
  )

sampled_no_results <- setdiff(sampled_sites$monitoring_location_id, site_check$monitoring_location_id)
if (length(sampled_no_results) > 0) {
  warning("sampled_locations.csv lists locations with no results this year (ignored): ",
          paste(sampled_no_results, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
}

site_check |>
  summarise(
    locations                          = n_distinct(monitoring_location_id),
    not_in_reference                   = sum(!in_reference),
    non_numeric_coords                 = sum(!numeric_ok),
    wrong_longitude_sign               = sum(!sign_ok),
    export_differs_from_registered     = sum(in_reference & !export_matches),
    sampled_location_differs_from_qapp = sum(sampled_differs),
    locations_with_several_coord_pairs = sum(duplicated(monitoring_location_id))
  )
```

Every count above should be zero except `sampled_location_differs_from_qapp`, which is informational (the registered location is still used for the upload). Each location with a problem or a sampled-location difference is listed below and written to `output/q28_coordinate_differences.csv`. Use the blank `notes` column to describe each one (where the crew sampled and why); a difference is documented, not fixed by adding a new location. Notes already in that file are kept when the document is re-rendered (matched on location ID and issue).

```{r q28-problems}
q28_path <- here("output/q28_coordinate_differences.csv")

coord_diffs <- site_check |>
  filter(!in_reference | !numeric_ok | !sign_ok | !export_matches | sampled_differs) |>
  mutate(
    issue = case_when(
      !in_reference   ~ "Location not registered in CDX",
      !numeric_ok     ~ "Non-numeric coordinates",
      !sign_ok        ~ "Longitude is not negative",
      !export_matches ~ "Export coordinates differ from registered coordinates",
      TRUE            ~ "Sampled location differs from QAPP-registered location"
    ),
    distance_m = case_when(
      sampled_differs ~ haversine_m(sampled_lat, sampled_lon, ref_lat, ref_lon),
      TRUE            ~ haversine_m(lat, lon, ref_lat, ref_lon)
    )
  ) |>
  select(monitoring_location_id, river_mile, issue,
         sampled_latitude = sampled_lat, sampled_longitude = sampled_lon,
         registered_latitude = ref_lat, registered_longitude = ref_lon, distance_m,
         sampled_note) |>
  arrange(monitoring_location_id)

# Carry over notes typed into a previous version of the file
coord_diffs$notes <- ""
if (file.exists(q28_path)) {
  old <- read_csv(q28_path, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
  if (all(c("monitoring_location_id", "issue", "notes") %in% names(old))) {
    prior <- old$notes[match(paste(coord_diffs$monitoring_location_id, coord_diffs$issue),
                             paste(old$monitoring_location_id, old$issue))]
    coord_diffs$notes <- coalesce(prior, "")
  }
}
# Seed empty notes from the user's sampled_locations.csv note
coord_diffs <- coord_diffs |>
  mutate(notes = if_else(notes == "" & issue == "Sampled location differs from QAPP-registered location",
                         coalesce(sampled_note, ""), notes)) |>
  select(-sampled_note)

write_csv(coord_diffs, q28_path)
coord_diffs
```

The table above is empty when every location passes (the CSV is then written with only its header row).

```{r q28-download}
#| results: asis
if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  uri <- paste0("data:text/csv;base64,", jsonlite::base64_enc(readBin(q28_path, "raw", file.size(q28_path))))
  cat(sprintf('<p><a download="q28_coordinate_differences.csv" href="%s">Download q28_coordinate_differences.csv</a></p>', uri))
}
```

The link above downloads the table as a CSV that you can fill in; to keep notes in the repo, edit `output/q28_coordinate_differences.csv` directly.

```{r q28-cue}

if (any(coord_diffs$issue == "Sampled location differs from QAPP-registered location")) {
  cat("::: {.callout-warning}\n## Action needed: sampled location differs from the QAPP\n\n",
      "For the location(s) below, the coordinates where crews sample differ from the coordinates ",
      "registered in CDX and listed in the QAPP. The upload uses the registered location. ",
      "Describe the difference where appropriate in this report (and in the `notes` column of ",
      "the CSV above). The QAPP site coordinates should be updated at the next QAPP revision.\n\n",
      paste0("- ", unique(coord_diffs$monitoring_location_id[
        coord_diffs$issue == "Sampled location differs from QAPP-registered location"]),
        collapse = "\n"),
      "\n:::\n", sep = "")
}
```

Reference sites with no results in this year's data (informational; planned-but-missing sites are handled in Q23):

**30.) Is all project metadata correct?**

The project metadata submitted to CDX is set in `config.yml` (`cdx:`) and written to `project.csv` and to the `Project ID` column of the results file by `generate_cdx_export.R`. The table shows what will be submitted, and the checks below test structure only (values present, ID numeric, URL form, and agreement with the WQP project record when that download is available).

```{r q30}
project_meta <- tibble(
  field = c("Project ID", "Project name", "QAPP approved", "QAPP approval agency",
            "Project description URL", "QAPP filename"),
  value = c(config$cdx$project_id, config$cdx$project_name, config$cdx$qapp_approved,
            config$cdx$qapp_approval_agency, config$cdx$project_description_url,
            config$cdx$qapp_filename) |> as.character()
)

wqp_project <- if (file.exists(wqp_project_file)) read_csv(wqp_project_file, show_col_types = FALSE) else NULL

project_checks <- tibble(
  check = c("All fields filled", "Project ID is numeric", "QAPP approved is Yes or No",
            "Description is a web address",
            "Project ID and name match the WQP project record"),
  passed = c(
    all(!is.na(project_meta$value) & nzchar(project_meta$value)),
    grepl("^[0-9]+$", as.character(config$cdx$project_id)),
    config$cdx$qapp_approved %in% c("Yes", "No"),
    grepl("^https?://", config$cdx$project_description_url),
    if (is.null(wqp_project)) NA else
      any(as.character(wqp_project$ProjectIdentifier) == as.character(config$cdx$project_id) &
            wqp_project$ProjectName == config$cdx$project_name)
```

**31.) Is the organization ID correct?**

The organization ID is set in `config.yml` (`cdx: organization_id`). WQX Web prepends it, followed by a hyphen, to every uploaded location and activity ID, so the upload files must carry bare IDs and the registered locations must already carry this prefix.

```{r q31}
org_id <- config$cdx$organization_id
org_prefix <- paste0(org_id, "-")

has_prefix <- function(x) !is.na(x) & startsWith(as.character(x), org_id)

org_checks <- tibble(
  check = c("Organization ID is set",
            "Every registered location in baseline_sites.csv starts with the organization ID",
            "No location ID in the export carries the prefix",
            "No activity ID in the export carries the prefix",
            "Organization ID matches the WQP project record"),

    !is.null(org_id) && !is.na(org_id) && nzchar(org_id),
    all(startsWith(read_csv(here("reference/baseline_sites.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)$MonitoringLocationIdentifier,
                   org_prefix)),
    !any(has_prefix(export_dat$monitoring_location_id)),

    if (is.null(wqp_project) || !"OrganizationIdentifier" %in% names(wqp_project)) NA else
      all(wqp_project$OrganizationIdentifier == org_id)
  )
)

tibble(organization_id = org_id, upload_prefix_added_by_wqx_web = org_prefix)
```

**32.) Are the time zones consistent and correct (AKDT in summer)?**

All sampling is in the Kenai watershed, so the correct zone follows from the date alone: AKDT from the second Sunday of March to the first Sunday of November, AKST otherwise (`akt_zone()` in `functions/clock_utils.R`, from the time zone database). The results file has no time zone columns. The WQX Web import configuration adds Activity Start and Analysis Start Time Zone as a constant (`cdx: import_config_time_zone` in `config.yml`, `AKDT` in the saved import configuration), so this check confirms that every activity and analysis date falls in that zone. If any date is AKST, the import configuration must be changed before upload.

```{r q32}
zone_tbl <- bind_rows(
  tibble(date_type = "Activity start", date = as.Date(export_dat$activity_start_date)),
  tibble(date_type = "Analysis start", date = ymd(export_dat$analysis_start_date))
) |>
  filter(!is.na(date)) |>
  distinct() |>
  mutate(expected_zone = akt_zone(date),
         import_config_zone = config$cdx$import_config_time_zone,
         consistent = expected_zone == import_config_zone) |>
  arrange(date_type, date)
zone_tbl

# Zone labels cannot show that the recorded clock times are local (a logger set to UTC would
# shift times by 8-9 hours), so activity start times are checked against a daytime window.
window_start_h <- 5
window_end_h <- 22

time_window <- export_dat |>
  mutate(start_hour = suppressWarnings(lubridate::hour(lubridate::hms(as.character(activity_start_time))))) |>
  filter(!is.na(start_hour)) |>
  summarise(n_with_time = n(),
            earliest_hour = min(start_hour), latest_hour = max(start_hour),
            n_outside_window = sum(start_hour < window_start_h | start_hour >= window_end_h),
            .by = activity_start_date) |>
  arrange(activity_start_date)
time_window
```

`n_outside_window` counts activity start times before 05:00 or at or after 22:00 (a plausibility window chosen for daytime field sampling, not a QAPP rule). Results with no recorded time are not counted.

```{r q32-stop}
if (any(!zone_tbl$consistent)) {
  stop("Q32: dates outside ", config$cdx$import_config_time_zone, ": ",
       paste(unique(zone_tbl$date[!zone_tbl$consistent]), collapse = ", "),
       ". Change the time zone constant in the WQX Web import configuration and config.yml.")
}
if (any(time_window$n_outside_window > 0)) {
  warning("Q32: some activity start times fall outside ", window_start_h, ":00-", window_end_h,
          ":00; check that clocks were set to local time.", call. = FALSE)
}
```

MANUAL: confirm that field and lab clocks were set to local Alaska time, and note any event close to a daylight-saving change (not yet written for this year).

**33.) Are all media types included? Media types appropriate to Characteristic?**

Every upload row carries the Activity Media Name set in `config.yml` (`wqx: activity_media_name`), and each Characteristic Name is checked against EPA's WQX Characteristic domain list (accepted names only). Both lists are copies of EPA's downloads in `reference/wqx_domains/` (downloaded `r config$wqx$domain_download_date`; see the README there). This program samples surface water only, so one media type is expected; the check confirms that the configured value is valid and that no row is blank or different.

```{r q33}
source(here("functions/check_wqx_domain.R"))

media_bad <- check_wqx_domain(export_dat$activity_media_name, "ActivityMedia")
char_bad <- check_wqx_domain(export_dat$characteristic_name, "Characteristic")

  check = c("Configured media name is in the WQX Activity Media list",
            "Every export row has a valid Activity Media Name",
            "Every export row has the configured media name",
            "Every Characteristic Name is an accepted WQX name"),
  passed = c(!is.null(media_cfg) && media_cfg %in% read_wqx_domain("ActivityMedia"),
             nrow(media_bad) == 0,
             all(export_dat$activity_media_name == media_cfg, na.rm = TRUE),
             nrow(char_bad) == 0)
)
q33_checks

export_dat |> count(activity_media_name, name = "n_results")
```

## Part D: CDX Export

```{r cdx-file-summary, message=FALSE}
cdx_files <- here("output", c("results_activities.csv", "project.csv", "station.csv"))
tibble(file = basename(cdx_files),
       rows = map_int(cdx_files, \(f) if (file.exists(f)) nrow(read.csv(f)) else NA_integer_))
```
